chunks: Upon the infidels -- which none would be able to repel --

key_terms.دَافِعٌ: A repeller / one who wards off
key_terms.لَيْسَ لَهُ: There is not for it / none has

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that nothing can repel the fate of the disbelievers?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah, illustrating that divine decree (Qadr) is inescapable for those who reject the truth, regardless of their worldly power or status. It serves as a reminder that intercession (Shafa'ah) is only effective by Allah's leave, rendering the disbelievers' own efforts futile against the inevitable outcome of their denial.
